title: Employment Agreement: Version 1 vs Version 2
disclaimer: FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT — NOT LEGAL ADVICE.
summary: Version 2 introduces significantly more restrictive terms for the employee in several key areas, while also offering improved salary, leave, and some new protections.
overallAssessment: Version 2 includes both positive changes (higher salary, better leave, new protection on training recovery for company-initiated termination) and more restrictive changes (longer notice period, extended confidentiality, extended non-solicitation, doubled training recovery cap, new auto-renewal clause).

changes.plainEnglishBefore: You needed to give 30 days' notice to resign.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: You must now give 90 days' notice to resign.
changes.whyItMatters: The notice period has tripled. A 90-day notice period means you cannot start a new role for approximately 3 months after deciding to leave. This is a significant change that affects career flexibility.
changes.textBefore: ...either party wishing to terminate this Agreement shall provide the other with thirty (30) days' written notice.
changes.textAfter: ...either party wishing to terminate this Agreement shall provide the other with ninety (90) days' written notice.

changes.plainEnglishBefore: You could owe a maximum of ₹1,00,000 for training recovery.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: You could owe up to ₹2,00,000 for training recovery if you resign within 24 months of training.
changes.whyItMatters: The maximum financial exposure for training recovery has doubled. This is a more significant financial commitment if you intend to leave within two years of completing company-funded training.
changes.textBefore: The aggregate training cost recovery obligation shall not exceed ₹1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh) in any instance.
changes.textAfter: The aggregate training cost recovery obligation shall not exceed ₹2,00,000 (Rupees Two Lakhs) in any instance.

changes.plainEnglishBefore: Confidentiality obligations lasted 2 years after employment ended.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: Confidentiality obligations now last 5 years after employment ends.
changes.whyItMatters: The confidentiality period has more than doubled. A 5-year post-employment restriction is substantially more limiting for future career opportunities, especially in the same industry.
changes.textBefore: ...shall remain in force for a period of two (2) years following the date of termination.
changes.textAfter: ...shall remain in force for a period of five (5) years following the date of termination.

changes.plainEnglishBefore: You could not approach company staff or clients for 12 months after leaving.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: You cannot approach company staff or clients for 18 months after leaving. Client lookback period also extended to 18 months.
changes.whyItMatters: The restriction period has increased by 50%. The extended lookback for client contact also widens the scope of the restriction.
changes.textBefore: ...for a period of twelve (12) months following termination...
changes.textAfter: ...for a period of eighteen (18) months following termination...

changes.valueAfter: Auto-renews annually unless 60 days' notice of non-renewal is given
changes.plainEnglishBefore: No automatic renewal clause existed in version 1.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: The contract now automatically renews every year on the anniversary of the start date. If neither party gives 60 days' written notice before the anniversary, the contract renews automatically.
changes.whyItMatters: This is an entirely new clause. Missing the 60-day notice window could result in being contractually committed for another year. The deadline for the first renewal notice is approximately 60 days before the first anniversary.
changes.textAfter: This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one-year periods on each anniversary of the Commencement Date, unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the relevant anniversary date.

changes.plainEnglishAfter: Annual CTC increased to ₹24 Lakhs — a 33% increase.
changes.whyItMatters: The salary has increased substantially. This is a significant positive change.
changes.textBefore: ...gross annual Cost to Company (CTC) of ₹18,00,000 (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs)...
changes.textAfter: ...gross annual Cost to Company (CTC) of ₹24,00,000 (Rupees Twenty-Four Lakhs)...

changes.plainEnglishBefore: Bonus was capped at 15% of basic salary.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: Bonus cap increased to 20% of basic salary.
changes.whyItMatters: A higher bonus cap is a positive change, though the bonus remains discretionary.
changes.textBefore: ...annual performance bonus of up to 15% of the basic annual salary...
changes.textAfter: ...annual performance bonus of up to 20% of the basic annual salary...

changes.plainEnglishAfter: 21 days paid annual leave — 3 additional days.
changes.whyItMatters: A modest but positive improvement to leave entitlement.
changes.textBefore: ...entitled to 18 days of paid annual leave per calendar year...
changes.textAfter: ...entitled to 21 days of paid annual leave per calendar year...

changes.textBefore: ...entitled to 8 days of paid sick leave per calendar year.
changes.textAfter: ...entitled to 10 days of paid sick leave per calendar year.

changes.plainEnglishBefore: Either party could terminate during probation with just 7 days' notice.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: Either party must now give 14 days' notice during probation.
changes.whyItMatters: Slightly increased protection during the probation period. This is a minor positive change.

changes.valueAfter: Must disclose pre-existing IP in writing before commencement
changes.plainEnglishBefore: No obligation to disclose existing personal IP before starting.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: You must proactively disclose any pre-existing IP you want to retain before you start.
changes.whyItMatters: Failure to disclose pre-existing IP could result in the company claiming ownership of it. If you have side projects or personal IP, you should disclose and agree exclusions before signing.
changes.textAfter: Prior to commencement, the Employee shall disclose to the Company in writing any pre-existing IP that the Employee intends to exclude from the scope of this clause.

changes.valueBefore: No protection — recovery applied regardless of who terminated
changes.valueAfter: Training recovery does not apply if company terminates employee (other than for cause)
changes.plainEnglishBefore: If you were let go by the company and had recently completed training, you could still owe training recovery.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: If the company decides to terminate your employment (other than for misconduct), you will not owe training recovery costs.
changes.whyItMatters: This is a meaningful new protection. Under version 1, even redundancy could trigger training cost recovery. This clause provides a fairer outcome.
changes.textAfter: Training cost recovery shall not apply where the Company terminates the Employee's employment other than for cause.

changes.valueBefore: Minimum 3 days per week in office
changes.valueAfter: Minimum 4 days per week in office
changes.plainEnglishBefore: You were required to come to the office at least 3 days per week.
changes.plainEnglishAfter: You are now required to come to the office at least 4 days per week.
changes.whyItMatters: A reduction in remote working flexibility. Working 4 days in the office instead of 3 limits work-from-home days to one per week.
